harnessExplanation.role: Tests.lawspec says what must be true. Solution implements the function. Harness.lawspec describes how to choose inputs for the generated property checks.
harnessExplanation.declaration: The first line names this harness, then for names the unit from Tests.lawspec that it tests. A strategy is a recipe for drawing values. :: introduces its type; where restricts its values; any asks the testing engine to generate values of that type. for law selects a named property, and use binds a strategy to one of its quantified inputs.
harnessExplanation.scope: A strategy changes the inputs sampled, not the requirement in Tests. A passing sample says only that the checks passed for the inputs tried. It is not a proof, and changing a generator to avoid a failure does not repair a bug or a false claim.
harnessExplanation.execution: The generated test runner is also called a harness. You edit the LawSpec configuration here; the compiler builds the runner that calls your implementation and records results. Run examples selects concrete and boundary checks; Run sampled property selects generated property cases; Run all checks includes both. Seed repeats generation under the same code, generator and tool versions; Replay failure also uses the recorded path to the failing case. F# runs through Fable and the JavaScript runner with fast-check in this browser, separately from native .NET/FsCheck.

stages.title: One example, one shortcut
story: We need addition. The first test asks for 1 + 2 = 3. Read the function beside this paragraph: it recognizes exactly that pair and returns zero for everything else.

stages.title: Ask whether order matters
story: Addition should give the same result when its inputs trade places. The quantified LawSpec property in Tests makes those two calls and requires equal results.

Where do the new inputs come from? Open Harness. A harness connects a law to a strategy: a recipe for test data. Here numbers chooses integers from -2 through 2. The two use lines feed separate draws into x and y of swapInputs. Tests supplies the comparison; the harness supplies its inputs.

The LawSpec strategy now supplies pairs between -2 and 2. The memorized implementation can return 3 for one order and 0 for the other. Run all checks to execute this LawSpec property against the actual implementation.

stages.syntax: In Harness, :: introduces the strategy’s type and where restricts its integers; any asks for generated values. for law swapInputs refers to the named law in Tests. use numbers for x supplies its quantified input x, and the next use supplies y. The claim permits -10 through 10, but this recipe samples only -2 through 2.
harnessNotes: numbers draws Int32 integers from -2 through 2, including both endpoints. The variable n describes each candidate value inside the strategy; it is not a separate input to add.

for law swapInputs selects the claim in Tests. use numbers for x and use numbers for y draw the two inputs separately from that recipe. The law permits -10 through 10; this strategy samples a smaller region, so a passing sample cannot establish the whole claim.

module Solution

let add (x: int) (y: int) : int =
    if x = 1 && y = 2 then 3
    elif x = 2 && y = 2 then 4
    else 0

module Solution

let sort (xs: int list) : int list = []
fsharp.Tests.lawspec:
-- ref:DEC-learn-tests-in-lawspec
unit learn.sorting
sort :: List Int32 -> List Int32

function ordered (xs :: List Int32) -> Bool is
  first matching case of xs :
    when Nil then true
    when Cons h t then
      (first matching case of t :
        when Nil then true
        when Cons next rest then h <= next and ordered t
      end case)
  end case
end function

law emptyInput is
  definition:
    sort [] = []
  end definition
end law

law sortingRule is
  definition:
    for all (xs :: List Int32) => ordered (sort xs) = true end for all
  end definition
end law

end unit
fsharp.Harness.lawspec:
harness learn.sorting.testing for learn.sorting is
  strategy number :: (n :: Int32 where n >= -20 and n <= 20) is any end strategy

  -- Draw up to three items constructively; shrinking follows these choices.
  strategy lists :: List Int32 is
    bind a :: Int32 from number in
      bind b :: Int32 from number in
        bind c :: Int32 from number in
          one of [], [a], [a, b], [a, b, c]
        end bind end bind end bind
  end strategy

  for law sortingRule
    use lists for xs
  end for law
end harness

module Solution

let sort (xs: int list) : int list = []
fsharp.Tests.lawspec:
-- ref:DEC-learn-tests-in-lawspec
unit learn.sorting
sort :: List Int32 -> List Int32

function ordered (xs :: List Int32) -> Bool is
  first matching case of xs :
    when Nil then true
    when Cons h t then
      (first matching case of t :
        when Nil then true
        when Cons next rest then h <= next and ordered t
      end case)
  end case
end function

law emptyInput is
  definition:
    sort [] = []
  end definition
end law

law sortingRule is
  definition:
    for all (xs :: List Int32) => ordered (sort xs) = true end for all
  end definition
end law

end unit

  strategy number :: (n :: Int32 where n >= -20 and n <= 20) is any end strategy

  strategy lists :: List Int32 is
    bind a :: Int32 from number in
      bind b :: Int32 from number in
        bind c :: Int32 from number in
          one of [], [a], [a, b], [a, b, c]
        end bind end bind end bind
  end strategy

  for law sortingRule
    use lists for xs
  end for law
end harness
